blocks.en: Abstract
blocks.zh: 摘要

blocks.en: Tracking a fast-moving point in 3D is prohibitive when RGB frames are blurred or too far apart to reveal its motion. Event cameras record brightness changes between frames, providing measurements inside these temporal gaps. We introduce TrackAnyMotion, which combines monocular RGB frames and events to track arbitrary points in 2D and 3D, including at times when no RGB frame is available. The motion expected for a static point, given scene geometry and camera motion, provides a reference for identifying independently moving objects. An independent-motion decoder combines geometric motion cues with event guidance and 2D tracks, feeding its predictions back into iterative 2D and 3D refinement. We also introduce HyperEvent, a synthetic RGB--Event dataset with high-frequency 3D trajectories, geometry, and independent-motion labels. At RGB frame timestamps on this benchmark, TrackAnyMotion reduces 3D and 2D endpoint errors by 70\% and 32\%, respectively.
blocks.zh: 当RGB框架模糊或相距太远而无法显示其运动时,跟踪3D中的快动点是令人无法接受的. 事件相机记录了相框之间的亮度变化,在这些时间间隔内提供测量. 我们引入 TrackAnyMotion,它结合了单相光的RGB帧和事件来跟踪2D和3D中的任意点,包括在没有RGB帧时. 一个静点的预期运动,给定了场景几何和相机运动,为识别独立移动的物体提供了参考. 一个独立-运动解码器结合了几何运动提示与事件引导和2D轨道,将它的预测反馈到迭代2D和3D的完善中. 我们还引入了HyperEvent,一个合成的RGB-Event数据集,有高频3D轨迹,几何和独立的运动标签. 在这个基准上的RGB帧时间戳上,TrackAnyMotion将3D和2D端点错误分别减少70\%和32\%.

blocks.en: 1 Introduction
blocks.zh: 导言

blocks.en: Tracking any point in 3D is fundamental for a vast variety of tasks spanning from robot imitation and policy learning [ 47 , 55 ] , dynamic reconstruction [ 51 , 23 ] , motion-controlled video generation [ 10 , 12 ] , and physical inference [ 21 , 3 , 57 ] .
blocks.zh: 跟踪3D中的任何一点对于从机器人模仿和政策学习[47、55]、动态重建[51、23]、运动控制的视频生成[10、12]和物理推论[21、3、57]等范围广泛的各种任务都是至关重要的。

blocks.en: Despite the recent success of 3D point trackers, these methods are fundamentally limited by the hardware or standard cameras. A point on a fast-moving object travels far in the blind-time between consecutive frames, inevitably motion-blurring and corrupting its own observations. Moreover, standard cameras notably suffer from a bandwidth-latency trade-off that limits their performance in such cases. At low bandwidth and low frame rates, fast-objects appear motion blurred, while at high frame rates, motion blur is minimized at the expense of high bandwidth.
blocks.zh: 尽管三维点追踪器最近取得了成功,但这些方法从根本上受到硬件或标准相机的限制. 一个快动物体的分点在相接相框相接相接相接的盲点时间中远行,不可避免地会移动-blurring并腐蚀自己的观察. 此外,标准相机明显受到带宽不适的取舍,限制了其在这种情况下的性能。 在低带宽和低帧速率下,快视物体显得运动模糊,而高帧速率下,以高带宽为代价将运动模糊最小化.

blocks.en:
Event cameras have been shown to be an ideal complement to standard cameras in addressing the bandwidth-latency trade-off [ 7 ] .
They are bio-inspired sensors that asynchronously measure per-pixel brightness changes with microsecond temporal resolution. Due to their working principle, they trigger events sparsely, often in correspondence of moving edges yielding minimal bandwidth and providing information between subsequent frames.
blocks.zh:
事件相机已被证明是标准相机解决带宽-相关性取舍的理想补充 [7].
它们是生物激发的传感器,同步测量每像素亮度随微秒时间分辨率而变化。 由于它们的工作原理,它们很少触发事件,往往在移动边缘产生最小带宽和提供后续帧之间信息时对应.

blocks.en:
Recent frame–event trackers such as TAPFormer [ 28 ] exploit event-based motion, demonstrating high-frequency 2D tracking between frames.
Yet until now, there exists no event-based 3D point tracker that leverages a set of monocular observations of events and frames to estimate the displacement of each point in a scene with high temporal resolution.
Moreover, existing methods typically resort to tracking a sparse set of points using complex hardware setups involving multiple cameras
blocks.zh:
最近的帧-事件跟踪器如TAPFormer [28] 利用基于事件的运动,显示帧之间的高频2D跟踪.
然而直到现在,还没有基于事件的三维点跟踪器能够利用一组对事件和框架的单相观测来估计在时间分辨率高的场景中每个点的位移.
此外,现有方法通常利用涉及多台相机的复杂硬件设置来跟踪为数不多的一组点。

blocks.en: To overcome existing methods, we propose the first 3D track-any-point method, which leverages the high temporal resolution of event cameras in combination with standard frames to estimate 2D and 3D point displacement at high frequency.
blocks.zh: 为了克服现有的方法,我们提出第一个3D轨-任意点方法,利用事件相机的高时分分辨率与标准相框结合,估计高频下2D和3D点位移.

blocks.en:
We use the expected motion for a static point as the reference for tracking and disentangling motion caused by independently moving objects and by the static background.
By fusing frames and event features and iteratively conditioning 2D and 3D updaters with event features, we are able to extrapolate the geometry of the scene as well as the 2D-3D point displacement with high frequency.
blocks.zh:
我们使用一个静态点的预期运动作为跟踪和分散由独立移动物体和静态背景引起的运动的参考.
通过引信相框和事件特性以及带有事件特性的迭代调取2D和3D更新器,我们能够以高频推导出场景的几何和2D-3D点移位.

blocks.en:
With this work, we introduce HyperEvent , a large scale simulated dataset consisting of high frequency ground truth of depth, 2D-3D tracks, poses, and interdependently moving objects. with events and frames.
To the best of our knowledge, this is the first dataset tailored for 3D tracking and independently moving object segmentation using events and frames.
blocks.zh:
有了这个作品,我们引入了HyperEvent, 一个由高频地面真能深度, 2D-3D 轨迹组成的大型模拟数据集, 构型, 以及相互依赖的移动对象。 还有事件和框架
据我们所知,这是第一个为3D跟踪和用事件和框架独立移动物体分解而定制的数据集。

blocks.en: Our tracker outperforms state-of-the-art baselines in both 2D and 3D tracking by 70% and 32%, respectively. Moreover, TrackAnyMotion enables scenarios that are inaccessible to standard frame-based cameras by tracking points at arbitrary timestamps in time, outperforming interpolation-based baselines by 2x in both 2D and 3D.
blocks.zh: 我们的追踪器在2D跟踪和3D跟踪中分别比最新基线高出70%和32%. 此外,TrackAnyMotion通过在时间上任意的时间戳跟踪点,使标准帧相机无法进入的场景,在2D和3D中都比插值基线多出2x.

blocks.en: With this work we make the following contributions: 1. We present TrackAnyMotion , a monocular RGB–event tracker that follows arbitrary query points in 2D and 3D, including at timestamps between RGB frames ( Secs. 3.2 and 3.3 ) 2. We introduce geometry-conditioned independent-motion reasoning within iterative tracking, using deviations from camera-induced motion to predict motion masks and feed their features back into 2D and 3D refinement ( Secs. 3.3 and 3.4 ) 3. We construct HyperEvent , a synthetic RGB–Event dataset with high-frequency 3D trajectories, geometry, and independent-motion labels for training and controlled evaluation.

blocks.en: 2 Related work
blocks.zh: 2 相关工作

blocks.en: Image-space trackers such as CoTracker3 [ 22 ] learn correspondences from synthetic supervision and pseudo-labelled real videos, and a growing family of methods lifts these correspondences into 3D. SpatialTracker [ 59 ] , DELTA [ 37 ] , TAPIP3D [ 61 ] and TrackingWorld [ 31 ] rely on depth estimated by a separate network, whereas SpatialTrackerV2 [ 58 ] , St4RTrack [ 6 ] , D4RT [ 62 ] and V-DPM [ 44 ] predict scene geometry and point motion jointly in a single feed-forward pass. Trace Anything [ 30 ] represents every trajectory as a B-spline in time, so that positions can be read off at any instant, and TrackCraft3R [ 36 ] and ReLift [ 42 ] start from the output of a reconstruction model and refine tracks on top of it. TrackEverything [ 20 ] extends dense tracking to videos of more than a thousand frames with a persistent world-space representation. Our tracking backbone is Track4World [ 32 ] , which predicts world-centric dense 2D and 3D flow and refines it with iterative updates in the style of RAFT [ 45 ] . All of these methods see only RGB frames and report positions at frame times. TrackAnyMotion adds the event stream of the same camera and predicts 2D and 3D positions in between frames.

blocks.en: Event cameras report per-pixel brightness changes asynchronously and with microsecond latency, so they observe how the scene moves while a frame camera is blind between exposures [ 7 ] . Early data-driven trackers followed frame-initialised features with events alone [ 34 ] , and ETAP [ 14 ] and MATE [ 15 ] extended this to tracking any point from an event stream. Combining both modalities, FE-TAP [ 29 ] , TAPFormer [ 28 ] and BlinkTrack [ 41 ] fuse frames and events to output 2D tracks well above the frame rate, and our event encoder follows the design of TAPFormer. Continuous-time formulations go one step further and model each pixel’s trajectory as a parametric curve that can be sampled at any time [ 9 , 49 ] , but the trajectories remain in the image plane. In 3D, EMoTive [ 48 ] and Han et al. [ 16 ] recover optical flow together with motion in depth from events, which yields a 3D motion field over a short horizon rather than persistent correspondences. The event-based trackers that do produce 3D trajectories need additional sensing: stereo events in E-3DTrack [ 25 ] , a rig of four RGB and two event cameras in MER-Tracker [ 2 ] , or a depth map as input in E-TraMamba [ 40 ] . We work with a single RGB camera and its co-located events, take no depth as input, and output long-range 3D tracks of arbitrary points at timestamps between frames.

blocks.en: Separating the motion a camera induces from the motion of objects is a long-standing problem, and the most common tool is a comparison between the observed motion and the rigid flow that camera motion alone would produce given the scene depth. GeoNet [ 60 ] introduced this decomposition for unsupervised depth and pose learning, treating the residual as object motion. Event-based methods adopted the same idea in several forms: through motion compensation and contrast maximization [ 43 ] , by learning depth, ego-motion and motion masks jointly [ 35 ] , or, in Un-EVIMO [ 53 ] , by thresholding the rigid-flow residual into pseudo-labels for an event segmenter. More recent learned segmenters feed ego-motion-compensated events and temporal attention to the network [ 11 ] , predict masks together with future motion to suppress events on moving objects [ 38 ] , or supervise boundary ownership alongside motion masks [ 18 ] . On the RGB side, DynOSeg [ 17 ] fuses a geometry-aware residual map with depth features, and Segment Any Motion [ 19 ] reads moving objects off long-range tracks. Trackers themselves have started to carry motion structure: SpatialTracker [ 59 ] and MoSE3 [ 4 ] learn rigidity embeddings for trajectories, and TrackEverything [ 20 ] classifies points as static or dynamic and refines only the dynamic ones. What these approaches share is that the residual, or the static-versus-dynamic decision, is computed once, as preprocessing, as pseudo-labels, or as a single routing step. In TrackAnyMotion the residual is a running quantity instead: we recompute it from the current depth, pose and track estimates inside every refinement iteration, and use it both to segment independently moving objects (IMOs) and to decide how much each update should trust the event evidence.

GeoNet [60] 引入了这种分解,用于无监督的深度并构成学习,将剩余部分作为物体运动处理. 基于事件的方法以多种形式采用了相同的想法:通过运动补偿和对比最大化[43],通过学习深度,自我-运动和运动口罩共同[35],或在Un-EVIMO[53]中,通过将刚性流余入一个事件分线器的伪标签来限定. 更近期的学习分会将自我-运动补偿的事件和时间关注反馈给网络[11],预测口罩与未来抑制移动物体事件的运动[38],或监督边界所有权与运动口罩[18]. 在RGB方面,DynOSeg [17] 将具有深度特征的几何感知后遗图引信,而分会 Any Motion [19] 读取从远程轨道上移动的物体. 跟踪器本身也开始携带运动结构:空间跟踪器[59]和MOSE3[4] 学习为轨迹所嵌入的刚性,以及 Track 万事通[20]将分被归类为静态或动态,并只精炼动态的分. 这些方法的共同点是,剩余部分或静态与动态决定是一次计算,作为预处理、伪标签或单一的路由步骤。 在TrackAnyMotion中,剩余部分是一个运行中的数量取而代之:我们从当前深度重算,在每一次改进迭代中提出并跟踪估计值,并用它来分割独立移动的物体(IMOs),以及决定每一次更新应在多大程度上信任事件证据。

blocks.en: 3 Method
blocks.zh: 3 方法

blocks.en:
Our method jointly estimates 2D and 3D point trajectories and independent-motion masks from monocular RGB frames and synchronized events.
Our central idea is to use camera-induced motion as a geometric reference within iterative tracking: deviations from this reference help identify independently moving points, whose learned motion features in turn condition trajectory refinement.
For timestamps without an RGB observation, event-conditioned pose and motion predictions supply the target geometry needed by the tracker. Fig. 2 summarizes these two mechanisms.

对于没有RGB观测的时间戳,事件有条件的姿势和运动预测提供了跟踪者所需要的目标几何. 图2概述了这两种机制。

blocks.en: 5 Conclusion and Limitations
blocks.zh: 5. 结论和限制

blocks.en:
We presented TrackAnyMotion, a monocular RGB–event tracker that recovers 2D and 3D point trajectories between RGB frames.
Its independent-motion feedback connects event measurements with scene geometry to guide iterative trajectory refinement.
We also introduced HyperEvent, providing synchronized frames, events, high-frequency trajectories, geometry, and independent-motion labels.
Together, these contributions advance point tracking beyond RGB sampling rates.
Reliance on monocular geometry and limited validation with real events remain limitations.

它的独立运动反馈将事件测量与场景几何连接起来,以指导迭代轨迹的完善.
我们还引入了HyperEvent,提供同步帧,事件,高频轨迹,几何,独立运动等标签.
这些捐款加在一起,先行点追踪超过了RGB取样率。
依赖单相几何和对实际事件的有限验证仍然是有限的。

The high-frequency tracking comparison in the main paper separates RGB observation timestamps

560,615 and 153,519 correspondence occurrences in the 2D evaluation, respectively.

independently moving objects and static regions. The 2D accuracy

blocks.en:
Each scene is simulated using PyBullet rigid-body physics. Objects first
settle under normal gravity. We then apply similarity time compression with a factor of k = 4 k=4 : linear and angular velocities are scaled by k k ,
gravity by k 2 k^{2} , and the simulation and rendering rates by k k . The
resulting trajectories satisfy x ′ ​ ( t ) = x ​ ( k ​ t ) x^{\prime}(t)=x(kt) , meaning that the scene follows
the same trajectory but evolves k k times faster. This produces the fast
motion that motivates the use of event cameras, while preserving per-frame
pixel displacement, frame count, and rendering cost.

blocks.en:
We generate events from the HR frames using the CUDA backend of the Event
Simulator (ESIM). Each frame is converted to log-luminance, L = log ⁡ ( 0.299 ​ R + 0.587 ​ G + 0.114 ​ B ) L=\log(0.299R+0.587G+0.114B) . Between consecutive HR frames, log-luminance
is assumed to vary linearly. An event is emitted when the interpolated
log-luminance crosses a contrast threshold of ± 0.2 \pm 0.2 relative to the
per-pixel reference. Event timestamps are obtained by linear interpolation
and stored in microseconds. The resulting events are sorted by timestamp.

blocks.en: D.2 Real-World Dataset
blocks.zh: D.2 实时世界数据集

blocks.en:
To construct a real-world dataset, we capture several fast-moving objects
using a calibrated and synchronized setup comprising a Prophesee Gen4 event
camera and a FLIR Blackfly S color camera operating at 10 fps. The dataset
has a spatial resolution of 945 × 649 945\times 649 and includes accurate camera
poses provided by a motion capture system. We use this dataset to
qualitatively evaluate our method on real-world scenes.

blocks.en: D.3 Time Lens Dataset
blocks.zh: D.3 时连数据集

blocks.en:
The High-Speed Event and RGB (HS-ERGB) dataset, introduced with
Time Lens [ 46 ] , contains real event streams and
high-speed color videos of dynamic indoor and outdoor scenes.
The recording setup combines a Prophesee Gen4 event camera
( 1280 × 720 1280\times 720 ) with a global-shutter FLIR Blackfly S RGB camera
( 1440 × 1080 1440\times 1080 ), separated by a 2.5 cm baseline and synchronized
in hardware. The recorded sequences use RGB frame rates of
150–163 Hz. They comprise close-range scenes with fast, nonlinear
object motion and distant scenes dominated by camera motion,
including spinning objects, bursting balloons, water splashes,
and rapid camera rotations.

blocks.en:
Spatial alignment uses stereo rectification, with an additional
feature-based homography for close-range planar scenes recorded
with a stationary camera. HS-ERGB complements our synthetic benchmark
with real sensor recordings of challenging motion. Its high-rate RGB
frames provide image references for frame-interpolation evaluation;
the original release does not include annotated 2D/3D point
trajectories or independent-motion masks. It therefore supports
qualitative assessment of our tracking and segmentation without
providing ground truth for their endpoint errors or mask IoU.
